pr_title: portAllocator sync local data before allocate
pr_body:
The port allocator method tries to allocate the ports directly
from the local memory instead from etcd.
It may happen, in deployments with multiple apiservers, that the
local port allocation information is out of sync, per example:

1. apiserver A create a service with NodePort X
2. apiserver B deletes the service
3. apiserver A creates the service again

If the allocation data of apiserver A wasn't refreshed with the
deletion of apiserver B, apiserver A fails the allocation because
the data is out of sync.

Don't try to do the Allocation operation locally first
and try them using etcd to avoid this issue.

issue_context.title: NodePort creation with statically assigned portNumber collide in multi-master HA cluster
issue_context.body:
Also reported in:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/32987
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/73140
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89042
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86104

**What happened**:
Service of NodePort type fails to (re)create if it was just deleted, and that delete had executed on different apiserver than the create is executing in.

**What you expected to happen**:
Service of NodePort type is created successfully.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Repeatedly create and delete service of NodePort type in a cluster that has more masters than one, and create/delete/create cycle hits two different masters:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: proxy
spec:
  ports:
    - name: "proxy"
      port: 443
      protocol: TCP
      targetPort: 443
      nodePort: 30443
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    service: proxy
```
used in a loop:
```
while kubectl -n default create -f test.yaml ; do kubectl -n default delete -f test.yaml; done
```

results in
```
service/proxy created
service "proxy" deleted
Error from server (Invalid): error when creating "proxy.yaml": Service "proxy" is invalid: spec.ports[0].nodePort: Invalid value: 30443: provided port is already allocated
```
if create/delete requests are load balanced to two different apiservers. It can be forced to happen by using two different kubeconfigs pointing to different apiservers for create and delete. In such case, first create and delete succeed, but second create fails, as it doesn't register the deletion the apiserver 2 did.


**Anything else we need to know?**:
This is a simplified test case. In our testing, when deleting and creating lots of objects (and create and delete happening on different apiservers), this does occur even "kubectl delete ... --wait=true" has finished successfully, and no objects are present. There seems to be some sort of time window where changes committed to one apiserver are not visible by another apiserver.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"15", GitVersion:"v1.15.5", GitCommit:"20c265fef0741dd71a66480e35bd69f18351daea", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T19:16:51Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"15", GitVersion:"v1.15.5", GitCommit:"20c265fef0741dd71a66480e35bd69f18351daea", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T19:07:57Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: local VMs
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): RHEL 7.7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): `Linux kubemaster1 3.10.0-1062.4.1.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Wed Sep 25 09:42:57 EDT 2019 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Install tools: custom
comments: /sig api-machinery

> There seems to be some sort of time window where changes committed to one apiserver are not visible by another apiserver.

That is correct. The port allocation map used to admit services is distributed to the API servers via etcd(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/rest/storage_core.go#L243-L252)

It appears the validation logic of a fixed node port first checks the local allocation map before persisting to etcd, so if an operation has not occurred that forced the local allocation map on another server to update from etcd, it will still think the port is reserved.

/remove-sig api-machinery
/sig network

/triage unresolved

Comment `/remove-triage unresolved` when the issue is assessed and confirmed.

I think I can confirm @liggitt's comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85894#issuecomment-562153133

If I understood the code correctly, the port allocator checks only the local map
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f70231ce7736cc748f76526c98955f86c667a41/pkg/registry/core/service/allocator/storage/storage.go#L83-L93

and if the local map has the port in use(because it wasn't updated), but etcd have it free (because it was deleted by other apiserver), 
the code returns and never checks etcd thus the error described in this issue.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f70231ce7736cc748f76526c98955f86c667a41/pkg/registry/core/service/allocator/bitmap.go#L87-L99

I've verified that checking if the port is allocated directly in etcd works without issues, you can checkout the following PR locally if you want to try

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86527

But since the original comment says 

> // Allocate attempts to allocate the item locally and then in etcd.

it seems that this is working as intended, git blame points to @justinsb , maybe he can expand on this.

Personally I think that writing directly to etcd is much expensive than implementing a retry logic in the client since the status code returned is a 422. Also, creating and deleting a nodePort constantly in a short period doesn't seems a common operation but I may be wrong here 😅 .

> Personally I think that writing directly to etcd is much expensive than implementing a retry logic in the client since the status code returned is a 422. Also, creating and deleting a nodePort constantly in a short period doesn't seems a common operation but I may be wrong here 😅 .

> This is a simplified test case. In our testing, when deleting and creating lots of objects (and create and delete happening on different apiservers), this does occur even "kubectl delete ... --wait=true" has finished successfully, and no objects are present. 

making it a very real problem, since kubectl doesn't show any objects left, yet it fails to create the nodeport. "Lots of objects" here means ~250.
I've submitted a PR that fixes the problem (I've tested it locally and can't reproduce the error), forcing the port allocator to sync with etcd before doing the allocation

Another reason you see this more in CI or other highly automated scenarios, is that the deletion of the services resources is done async via releaseAllocatedResources:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.18/pkg/registry/core/service/storage/rest.go#L265

So the service is fully removed, but allocated resources like the ClusterIP and NodePort are not. Generally, this is ok for the ClusterIP, but not the NodePort, if you're looking to quickly recreate them.
